bear_case.title: The whole SMR group is making new lows
bear_case.description: Oklo ($27.97), NuScale ($5.83), X-energy ($10.36) and Centrus ($114.94) all sold off hard Oct 14-16, several at fresh 52-week lows, despite a licence milestone (Clinch River) and record long-term uranium prices. Good news is not holding, which says valuation and dilution — not headlines — are driving the group. Counter: sharp drawdowns also reset entry prices, and the NRC permit is a real de-risking step.

bear_case.title: Dilution is the real funding model
bear_case.description: Oklo's ~$1B ATM, NuScale's $750M ATM and Centrus's $500M share offering mean each upbeat announcement can be financed by selling stock into it. Counter: raising capital is how pre-revenue builders fund long-lead projects, and the cash gives them runway.

bear_case.title: A construction permit is not an operating reactor
bear_case.description: The NRC's Sep 29 Clinch River permit authorizes construction only; there are still zero commercial SMRs operating, and NuScale's 6 GW TVA/ENTRA1 framework has no signed PPA more than a year on. Counter: TVA is moving through the licensing sequence ahead of schedule (14 months, four months early).

bear_case.title: Physical uranium is strong but equities are not following
bear_case.description: Long-term uranium at $97/lb is a 19-year high, yet Cameco is ~36% below its high, URNM is ~49% below its 52-week high and SPUT trades at a ~13% discount to NAV — the market is not paying for the fuel-price tailwind, and Westinghouse's IPO value is contested (~C$30.8B to $50B+ EV, window possibly to 2029). Counter: a widening gap can also close from the equity side.

bear_case.title: Hyperscaler money is going to old reactors, not new designs
bear_case.description: Google's 890 MW and Amazon's 690 MW deals both sit on Constellation's existing fleet and uprates, with new capacity only in the 2028-2032 window — which favours operators over pre-revenue SMR developers, and gas and renewables remain faster to build.
